entities.summary: Louis (de) Verjus, count of Crécy, was a French politician and diplomat who played a crucial role in the governance of Western Europe during the 17th century. Born into a noble family, Verjus rose to prominence through his strategic marriages and military appointments, eventually becoming a key advisor to the French monarch. His influence extended to the diplomatic sphere, where he navigated the complex web of alliances and rivalries between European powers. Verjus's legacy can be seen in the Treaty of Ryswick, which he helped negotiate in 1697, securing a temporary peace between France and its European enemies. Despite his significant contributions, Verjus's life was marked by controversy and personal scandal, which have only recently been subject to scholarly investigation. Verjus's story serves as a testament to the intricate and often fraught world of early modern European politics.
